quizName: DMV Practice Test #8 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What is a good way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Speed up.
Allow them to pass you.
Make gestures at them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow them to pass you.
questions.explanation: Let the tailgater pass you. If you speed up, they will just tailgate you at the higher speed, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: At night, how can you tell if there are bumps on the road ahead when riding behind another vehicle?

options.text: Listen for the other vehicle scraping against the pavement.
Watch the other vehicle's taillights bounce up and down.
Look at the rear bumper to see if it bounces.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch the other vehicle's taillights bounce up and down.
questions.explanation: Watch the vehicle ahead of you at night. If its taillights bounce up and down, there are bumps on the road.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection, a motorcyclist should NOT:

options.text: Choose a lane position that increases their visibility.
Speed up to cross the intersection quickly.
Cover the clutch and brakes to reduce reaction time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to cross the intersection quickly.
questions.explanation: Approach intersections slowly. Choose a lane position to be seen by other drivers. Cover the clutch and brakes to stop quickly. Do not speed up or change speed suddenly, as this confuses other drivers.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle stopped on the side of the road with flashing lights. What should you do?

options.text: Stop on the roadway behind the emergency vehicle.
Stop and wait until the emergency vehicle moves.
Move to a different lane away from the emergency vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to a different lane away from the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: Change lanes to move away from the emergency vehicle. Slow down and be ready to stop. Give the emergency vehicle extra space.

questions.question: What should you do to avoid fatigue on a long trip?

options.text: Drink coffee.
Limit how much you ride each day.
Play loud music.

questions.correctAnswerText: Limit how much you ride each day.
questions.explanation: Take frequent breaks to rest on long trips. Do not ride for more than six hours a day. Dress to protect yourself from wind, cold, and rain, as these make you tired faster.

questions.question: If a motorcycle is towing a trailer, the following distance should:

options.text: Increase.
Decrease.
Stay the same.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase.
questions.explanation: When towing a trailer, increase your following distance. The trailer adds weight, so your motorcycle needs more time to stop.

questions.question: What does a solid red arrow on a traffic signal mean?

options.text: You must come to a complete stop.
You may proceed with caution.
You must yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a red traffic light. You must stop and wait for a signal that allows you to turn in that direction.

questions.question: A motorcycle's brake light is _________ a car's brake light.

options.text: More noticeable than
Just as noticeable as
Not as noticeable as

questions.correctAnswerText: Not as noticeable as
questions.explanation: Your motorcycle's brake light is usually not as noticeable as a larger vehicle's brake light, especially when your taillight is on. Other drivers may not see your brake light.

questions.question: What is the best way to stay safe while riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Look well ahead of your motorcycle.
Avoid busy traffic areas.
Ride faster than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look well ahead of your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Always look far ahead on the road. Watch for hazards before you reach them so you can react in time.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow traffic light mean?

options.text: The light is about to turn red.
The light is about to turn green.
Stop and wait for traffic to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The light is about to turn red.
questions.explanation: A yellow light warns that the signal is changing to red. Slow down and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection, continue through.

questions.question: When does a motorcycle have less traction for braking?

options.text: When a motorcycle is leaning.
When a motorcycle is straight up and down.
When a motorcycle is on dry pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: When a motorcycle is leaning.
questions.explanation: A leaning motorcycle has less traction available for braking. This happens during turns and curves. You can use both brakes while turning, but you must be very careful.

questions.question: When you use alcohol and drugs together, what happens?

options.text: They are less dangerous than using either one alone.
They balance each other out.
Their effects can be stronger than using either one alone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Their effects can be stronger than using either one alone.
questions.explanation: Many drugs, including prescription and over-the-counter medicines, can make it harder to ride safely. When mixed with alcohol, these drugs become even more dangerous.

questions.question: When stopping your motorcycle with a passenger, what should you do?

options.text: Ride a little faster than normal.
Begin slowing down earlier than normal.
Merge into smaller traffic gaps than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Begin slowing down earlier than normal.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds extra weight to your motorcycle. This extra weight makes the motorcycle slower to respond. It takes longer to speed up, slow down, and turn. Start slowing earlier, reduce your speed, and look for larger gaps in traffic.

questions.question: Which lane position best stops other vehicles from sharing your lane?

options.text: The left side of the lane.
The center of the lane.
The right side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The center of the lane.
questions.explanation: Riding in the center of your lane discourages other drivers from trying to squeeze into your lane. When you ride behind a car, riding in the center makes you more visible in the vehicle's rearview mirror.

questions.question: How should you park a motorcycle in a parallel parking space next to a curb?

options.text: Position the motorcycle at an angle with the rear wheel to the curb.
Position the motorcycle at an angle with the front wheel to the curb.
Position the motorcycle on the grass, away from the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Position the motorcycle at an angle with the rear wheel to the curb.
questions.explanation: Park at an angle with the rear wheel toward the curb. Note that some cities require motorcycles to be parked parallel to the curb.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protect?

options.text: Your face, but not your eyes.
Your eyes, but not your whole face.
Your whole face.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your whole face.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face, including your eyes, in a crash. A windshield is not enough protection.

questions.question: What is a main cause of single-vehicle motorcycle crashes?

options.text: Riding too fast for the weather.
Turning too wide in a curve or turn.
Running off the road to avoid another vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turning too wide in a curve or turn.
questions.explanation: A main cause of single-vehicle crashes is turning too wide. When you turn too wide, your motorcycle can leave the road or hit an object.

questions.question: When stopping, which brakes should you use?

options.text: Both brakes.
The front brake only.
The rear brake only.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop. Using both brakes helps you stop quickly.

questions.question: Which is NOT a benefit of keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles?

options.text: You will have time to react to hazards.
You will have space to maneuver.
You will have more time to accelerate when entering a curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will have more time to accelerate when entering a curve.
questions.explanation: Keeping space around your motorcycle helps you react and maneuver if someone makes a mistake. This is not related to accelerating in curves.

questions.question: When making a U-turn, what should you do about the front brake?

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes at the same time.
Do not use the front brake because it could cause the bike to tip over.
Use the front brake to keep the motorcycle stable.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the front brake because it could cause the bike to tip over.
questions.explanation: Do not use the front brake during a U-turn because it can cause the bike to tip over. Use the rear brake instead to control your speed.

questions.question: Your lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Make it easier for others to see you.
Help you avoid road hazards.
Encourage other drivers to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Encourage other drivers to share your lane.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps others see you and lets you see them. It helps you avoid wind, blind spots, and road hazards. Your position should discourage other drivers from entering your lane and give you a way to escape if danger appears.

questions.question: When traveling in a group, riders should generally be:

options.text: In a single-file line.
In pairs.
In a staggered formation.

questions.correctAnswerText: In a staggered formation.
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is the best way for riders to stay close together while keeping safe space around each rider. Use a single-file line when taking curves, turning, entering a highway, or leaving a highway.

questions.question: When riding in the rain, you should:

options.text: Ride down the center of your lane.
Ride on the right side of your lane.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: Roads are very slippery when rain starts. Ride in tire tracks left by cars to get the best grip.

questions.question: When riding in a group on a straight road, motorcyclists should:

options.text: Ride in a single-file line.
Ride in pairs.
Use a staggered formation.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use a staggered formation.
questions.explanation: A staggered formation keeps the group close while giving each rider enough safe space. Switch to a single-file line when turning, riding curves, or entering or leaving a roadway.

questions.question: When preparing to ride with a passenger, instruct the passenger to:

options.text: Get on the motorcycle before you do.
Sit as far back as possible.
Hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.
questions.explanation: Have your passenger wait to get on until after you start the engine. They should sit as far forward as comfortable and hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.
